themes_detail.label: Missed Garbage Collection Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Missed garbage collection complaints spiked to 8 this week—a 357% increase over the 1.8 weekly average of the prior 8 weeks—signaling a potential sanitation breakdown in Brownsville/Ocean Hill this week.
evidence: 8 missed collection complaints filed this week vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (357% spike, z-score: 4.0)
Statistically significant anomaly suggests systemic service failure, not isolated incidents
Spike is acute and current (this week), not retroactive, indicating active ongoing problem
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if a collection route was suspended, truck shortage occurred, or labor shortage disrupted service this week
Interview residents on affected blocks about how long trash has been piling up and health/rodent impacts
Compare this week's spike to historical missed collection patterns to assess if this is weather-related or structural

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage and obstruction complaints surged this week: missing signs up 500% (3 vs. 0.5 weekly average), dangling signs up 540% (4 vs. 0.6 weekly average), and obstructions up 300% (4 vs. 1.0 weekly average), suggesting accelerated street-level infrastructure decay.
evidence: Street Sign - Missing: 3 complaints this week vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Street Sign - Dangling: 4 complaints this week vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 3.4)
Obstruction: 4 complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 3.46)
All three signals emerging in same week suggests concentrated street maintenance failure
reporting_angles: Map the geographic concentration of these complaints—are they clustered on specific avenues or blocks?
Contact DOT to determine if street maintenance crews have been reallocated or if budget cuts are delaying repairs
Assess whether dangling/missing signs create traffic safety hazards or confusion for residents

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints quadrupled this week to 4 complaints versus a 0.6 weekly baseline (540% spike, z-score: 3.94), indicating potential widespread tree disease, storm damage, or neglect in the district's urban canopy.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints this week vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 3.94)
Acute spike concentrated in single week suggests event-driven cause (recent storm, disease outbreak, or maintenance gap)
Tree complaints historically low baseline—spike is statistically prominent
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to investigate whether recent weather (high winds, disease) has triggered tree loss
Field-report on specific streets to document visible tree damage and assess whether dead trees pose safety risks (falling branches, root damage)
Interview residents about whether tree removal/maintenance requests have gone unaddressed

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Sustained
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints remained elevated 2 weeks ago at 7 complaints—a 250% spike over the 2.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.33)—suggesting ongoing resident concern about unlicensed or non-compliant cannabis operations in Brownsville/Ocean Hill.
evidence: 7 cannabis retailer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average (250% spike, z-score: 3.33)
Spike is 2 weeks old (not this week), suggesting sustained rather than acute concern
Pattern may reflect illicit vs. legal retail operations or licensing enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Map the locations of these complaints to identify clusters of unlicensed or problematic retailers
Contact NYC Office of Cannabis Management to determine licensing status of flagged retailers and enforcement actions
Interview residents about the nature of complaints (odor, loitering, unlicensed operation) and how they impact neighborhood quality of life

themes_detail.label: Water Leak Service Decline
themes_detail.summary: Water leak complaints dropped 72% this week to 7 complaints versus a 25.5 weekly average (z-score: -3.3), a statistically significant decline that may reflect either reduced reporting, service improvements, or a data collection issue worth investigating.
evidence: 7 water leak complaints this week vs. 25.5 weekly average (72% decline, z-score: -3.3)
Statistically significant downward anomaly is rare and unexpected in infrastructure complaint data
Decline could signal system improvements, seasonal pattern, or reporting lag
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to determine if water main repair work was completed this week
Verify whether the decline is real service improvement or a data reporting delay/backlog issue
Cross-reference with plumbing complaints (521 over 90 days) to assess whether water issues are shifting to different complaint categories
